Only when the water level drops do you often realize that your aquarium has a leak. While water always evaporates, if the water level is obviously decreasing, a leak could be a good reason for it. If you have a significant leak, the spot will be very obvious, so a quick inspection of the aquarium should help locate the leak. If the leak is not obvious, you might only notice it when you find a wet spot near your aquarium. Even a small damp area could indicate that there is a problem. If you have changed the filter, added new items to your aquarium, or made other changes, these could have caused the water to leak. Try to dry the area and observe if more water is leaking. If you see water outside the aquarium again, it is likely a leak. If you suspect a leak but do not find the spot immediately, you will need to search a bit. Look for metal corners that may have come loose from the glass. Another clue might be sealant that is obviously oozing out at the corners. These are telltale signs that there is a problem with your aquarium. Feel around the edges of the aquarium. If you feel wet glass, move your hand from that spot upwards until you feel the glass is dry. The wet spot closest to the top of the aquarium is likely the leak you are looking for. Once you find the leak or suspect a location, you should mark the area with a felt-tip pen. This way, you will know exactly where to begin your repairs once you have drained the water from your aquarium. After completing your repairs, the felt-tip markings can easily be removed with glass cleaner. Leaks along the seams can be relatively easy to fix, as they are usually due to sealing errors and seams can simply be resealed with silicone. However, if the leak is due to cracked glass, it is not so easily repaired. Replacing an entire pane of glass takes much more time and skill. In fact, it is very likely that such a repair can only be done by someone with the appropriate experience. If a side or the bottom of your aquarium is cracked, it is very likely that the entire aquarium will break. Before you can apply for Japanese citizenship, you must have lived in Japan for at least five consecutive years. You can also obtain Japanese citizenship if you meet one of the following conditions: You have lived in Japan for three or more years and are the child of a Japanese citizen. You were born in Japan and have lived there for at least three consecutive years, and either your father or mother was born in Japan. You have lived in Japan for ten or more consecutive years. You must not only prove when you lived in Japan but also provide all the times you left and re-entered Japan during that period. You can demonstrate this with copies of passports, visa documentation, or other similar official documents. However, each case is reviewed individually, meaning you may still receive Japanese citizenship with a criminal past. If you are married and your spouse provides for the family income, this requirement is met. If you are employed and specify your employer in your application, immigration officials may visit your workplace to verify the information you provided. In some countries, you must renounce your previous citizenship when applying for or during the process of obtaining Japanese citizenship. Japan does not allow dual citizenship to avoid potential conflicts of interest. It is possible to obtain Japanese citizenship without renouncing your own if you can prove extraordinary circumstances justifying it. Individuals younger than 20 can hold dual citizenship but must choose one nationality before turning 20. If you believe you meet all or most of the requirements for Japanese citizenship, you should contact the local Ministry of Justice in Japan, which will arrange a meeting. The first conversation can be conducted either by phone or in person and serves as a preliminary selection. The agency wants to ensure that you meet all or most of the requirements for obtaining Japanese citizenship. If you convince the official that you can proceed with your application, a second conversation will be scheduled. In this second conversation, you will learn about additional conditions you need to fulfill to determine your eligibility for Japanese citizenship. There is no fixed list of requirements; authorities examine each applicant and case individually, creating a requirement list based on this. Generally, you will need to submit the following types of documents: birth certificate, marriage certificate, passport, proof of international travel, employment verification, proof of assets, proof of residence, proof of education (transcripts, diplomas), proof of physical and mental suitability, and proof of no criminal record. During the second conversation, you will be shown a video about how to settle and integrate into Japan, lasting about an hour. After the second conversation, you will receive a list of specific documents you need to provide, along with a book outlining the naturalization requirements. You must read this book and begin gathering the required documents, which can take several months. Once completed, you can contact your caseworker at the agency to arrange an application interview. At the end of the second conversation, you will receive the name of your caseworker and your case number. If you believe you have met all the requirements, contact your caseworker to arrange an application interview (everything up to this point was just preparation). You will now meet with one or more officials who will review every detail of your application. If any points are missing or incomplete, you must submit them. It is also possible that during this interview, it will be determined that you need to provide additional documents. After submitting your application, you will be sent home to wait for the outcome. The officials will review and verify all details of your application, which may include a visit to your home. They are also authorized to inquire about your personal contacts or employers. During the verification process, you may be contacted to provide further information on any aspects of your application. This part of the application process can take several months. If everything is satisfactory to the authorities, you will be contacted for a final interview. At this interview, you will need to sign the required affidavits, and your application will be officially recognized by the agency. The immigration office will forward your completed citizenship application along with your signed statements to the Ministry of Justice. If the ministry maintains and confirms your documents, you will officially receive Japanese citizenship.

There are various ways to determine "who's turn it is." For example: the youngest player goes first; or the person whose birthday is next; or you can use a counting rhyme like "Ene Mene Muh" or the classic "Eckstein, Eckstein, everyone must be hidden." Or simply draw numbers from a hat, with "1" starting first. If one person is older than all the others, they are a natural choice. The younger you are, the quicker you may become frustrated if others are very well hidden. Older individuals tend to have a longer attention span and can think unconventionally compared to their younger peers. Once it’s determined who starts, that person remains at the starting point and begins counting aloud and at a steady pace to 10. Or 20, 50, or 100 – or they could recite a rhyme or sing a song. Anything that takes a bit of time until everyone else is hidden. Decide beforehand what it will be so everyone knows how long they roughly have. Make sure that the person doesn’t cheat! The person whose turn it is must have their eyes closed, hands over their eyes, and stand in a corner. No peeking! All players who are not “it” run off and hide quietly from the seeker. The person who is “it” cannot see where you are hiding. Be as quiet as possible; otherwise, the seeker can hear where you are hiding or in which direction you might be. Once you find a good hiding spot, stay quiet and still. Once you are hidden, you must not give yourself away! If you make noise, not even the best hiding place can conceal you. When the person who is “it” finishes counting, they shout “1-2-3, I’m coming!” Now they have to try to find all the other players. Both your eyes and ears should be alert, seeker! If you find someone, clearly mark them. Players hiding can change their position or leave their hiding place if they want. For example, it’s a good idea to change positions and hide in a place the seeker has already searched. That’s strategy! If some of the hidden players are not found after a certain amount of time or do not return to the starting point, the seeker should give the "all clear" signal. They can call out something like "Everyone is free." Then it is safe for the remaining players to come out. The one who was found first is "it" in the next round. You can play so that only one needs to be found to start a new round, or that all must be found. You can also introduce a time limit. If the seeker has not found everyone within the time limit after 3 tries, the seeker changes anyway. Give everyone a chance to hide!

Buy feed that is specifically tailored to the needs of laying hens. The feed should have a high content of plant fats and proteins. Remember that additional starch (from kitchen scraps or grains) must be supplemented with more protein, as it lowers the average protein content of the diet. If your hens have a calcium deficiency, they cannot produce strong eggshells. If the shells are weak and break when a hen sits on or steps on the egg, the hen will eat the damaged egg. Once she discovers that the egg contains proteins and fats, along with essential calcium in the shell, she will start breaking the egg and intentionally eating it. Other hens will observe her behavior and follow her example. Ground oyster shells or limestone are great sources of calcium for your hens. Mix one kilogram of this powder with 45 kilograms of feed, or provide your hens with an additional feeder from which they can eat. To increase calcium intake over several days, offer your hens a dish of whole milk. Avoid using eggshells as a calcium source for your hens, as they may recognize or smell them and start eating their eggs. If you choose this method, you should grind the shells into tiny pieces so that the hens cannot recognize what they are eating. You may notice that eggshells are softer in warm weather. Hens can store calcium less effectively in hot weather, so increase the additional calcium dosage in their feed on warm days. Even if hens have enough calcium available, a lack of water can cause them to consume the moisture from the eggs. Hens need more water than most other birds, so ensure they always have fresh, clean drinking water. You can add a vitamin supplement to the water that improves calcium absorption in your hens.

It is best to start rooting your hibiscus cuttings during the summer months (May, June, and July). Note that not all cuttings will develop roots, so you should always plant more cuttings than you need. You can generally expect that one-third or at best half of all cuttings will develop into viable plants. Take a 12 cm long shoot from your garden yew. Choose new, healthy shoots that are 12 cm long, and cut them at a 45-degree angle. The shoots should not be woody but soft and green, yet relatively sturdy. They need to be new shoots from this year and not old, woody ones. Remove the lower leaves from the shoots. Dip the cut end of the shoots in rooting hormones or cover them with rooting powder. Now, you need to decide how to root your cuttings, either in compost soil or in water. If you want to start rooting your cuttings in compost soil, stick the stems about 4 to 5 cm deep in a pot filled with moist compost soil. It is best to use compost soil or a mixture that is half compost soil and half sand. Cover the pot with a plastic bag or use an upside-down clear plastic bottle with the spout cut off to create a mini greenhouse. If you use a plastic bag, make sure it does not touch the cuttings. If necessary, you can hold the bag up with a small stick. Keep the potted cuttings moist and do not place them directly in the sun. They should start rooting after about a month or two. Some gardeners do not use compost soil; they prefer to place their cuttings in a clear glass or plastic container with water to allow roots to develop. If you do it this way, you can see the roots grow. Fill the glass or plastic container with 5 cm of water, place your cutting inside, and put it in a bright spot, but not directly in the sun. Cover it with a plastic bag and spray it daily with water from a spray bottle. It is important to place each cutting in a separate container to prevent bacteria from building up. Do this even if you are preparing multiple cuttings as recommended, so you have enough in case they do not root. If you place the cuttings from your hibiscus bush in water, remember to change the water regularly; every two to three days is advisable. It is recommended to use rainwater if possible. If you do not collect rainwater in your garden and do not have access to a stream, you could let tap water sit in a jug for 24 hours. This will remove some chlorine from the tap water. However, this is not strictly necessary, and your cuttings could also root in tap water. After you see new roots that are 2.5 to 5 cm long, plant the cutting in moist compost soil. They should not be exposed to direct sunlight for a few months. By then, the roots will be better established.

It is often difficult to accept, but some friendships are not worth saving. If your friend has constantly treated you poorly or you feel bad in their presence, you might want to say goodbye to them. Friends should treat each other kindly, encourage one another, respect each other, and have understanding. If either of you is unable to do this, then you probably do not have a healthy friendship. If you have to pretend to be someone else around that friend, it is a sure sign of a toxic friendship. If you always have to tread carefully around them, it is likely not a good friendship. If your friend constantly criticizes your personality, then you are in a toxic relationship. A good friend offers criticism compassionately. In a healthy, balanced friendship, both parties maintain contact with one another. However, if your friend never calls or texts you first, or if all plans originate from you, there may be an imbalance in your friendship. With a toxic friend, you might always have to fight for their attention and affection. A good friend accepts you as you are and takes time for you—without exceptions. Toxic people often try to make you set aside your own problems to focus on theirs. Remember how you felt in the presence of this person, and ask yourself if being friends with them was truly helpful and beneficial. You should feel that you can fundamentally trust your friend, and that you are there for each other. Your friend should support you on your path, and you should do the same for them. If you conclude that your friendship is not worth your efforts, then you must completely sever the connection with this person. Proceed with determination and honesty. Don’t just block their number and avoid them forever—end your friendship in person to provide closure. You could say something like, “I’ve been thinking about our friendship, and I believe I need a break. I don’t like how I feel when we are together. I think I need to clarify some things for myself.”

Before you banish people from your life, you should be sure to do it for the right reasons. Are you stressed? Are your friends stressed? If so, it may not be a good time. However, if this has been the case for a while and you no longer feel comfortable in their presence, it’s likely the right decision. Life is too short to spend time with people who do not bring out the best in us. Knowing exactly why you no longer wish to maintain the friendship will help you explain to the other person or people why you want to end the relationship. If you are convinced of your arguments, it is much harder to start a discussion and become angry. Do not act out of a bad mood or anger. If you are considering ending the friendship, sleep on it. If your feelings haven’t changed the next day, it’s probably sensible to go through with your decision. It may be hard at first to express your true feelings about the broken friendship, but in the long run, it’s the kindest thing you can do in this situation. It can also save you further stress in declaring the friendship over. Bring up the topic gently. Make sure not to blame the other person or accuse them of having an unbearable character. This is also somewhat about you. You might say something like: “I don’t know how you see the situation, but I’m willing to hear your thoughts. However, it’s important that you understand I feel our friendship isn’t working well anymore. I’m noticing more and more that we’ve developed in different directions (growing apart, constantly bickering, dragging each other down, etc.), and after thinking about it intensively, I believe we cannot save our relationship. I think we should see each other less and honestly admit what has happened to our friendship.” Be aware that you should remain objective and, as much as possible, not assign blame to anyone if you provide concrete reasons for the end of your friendship. As soon as you provide a reason that directly relates to the character or actions of the other person, you leave room for them to promise to change. This risks drawing you into a discussion from which it is difficult to extricate yourself. Focus on yourself and how you feel—things that no one can influence. To avoid a defensive response, keep your arguments neutral. You want to leave the situation with your head held high. Do not say anything negative about your friend’s character; this leads to defensiveness and can make you seem mean and petty. If that happens, you may feel compelled to “repair” the friendship, and it could take months before you feel strong enough to try to end the relationship again. Criticize how you feel in the friendship instead of addressing your friend’s annoying habits. You don’t want her to feel attacked—that can lead to nothing good (especially if you share mutual friends). Be aware that what you say will likely be interpreted negatively. This is completely human and a way to cope with the pain. So keep your statements simple, kind, and clear. This is not about being “convinced” that the friendship still makes sense, but about showing the decency to listen. You can summarize your friend’s description and then reiterate that you still feel the friendship has run its course. This conversation will likely lead to a lot of sadness, pain, or even anger from your friend. Be prepared to acknowledge these feelings, but do not let them tempt you to sweep the problems under the rug. Do not let yourself be insulted; angry reactions are a sign that a break is needed. If there is no conclusion, that’s okay. You have done what you needed to do. If your friend becomes angry during the conversation, do not feel tempted to explain your views. Simply repeat that you do not wish for a close friendship anymore. Emotions will run high, so it is important to remain as consistent as possible. In some cases, both of you will realize that your friendship has not been going anywhere for some time. Your friend will likely have the same feelings and be glad that you shared them honestly—so give it a try. You should not feel stuck in a friendship you are not interested in. Since you handled the situation openly and honestly, both of you know where things stand. It will be easier for both of you to deal with each other in the future if that becomes necessary. However, if that is not possible, the next part discusses the option of ending a friendship indirectly and passively.

Remember, you deserve a friendship that brings out the best in you.

Many European countries, such as Germany, England, and Ireland, have establishments called pubs or taverns where people drink. Unlike bars in America, pubs are restaurants with table service where people spend time, play pub quizzes, or go with their families. While some pubs have extensive cocktail menus, the main drinks served are beer, wine, and cider. You can spend the whole night in a pub eating with friends and listening to a local band. Pubs are so popular that there are some in America as well. Look for a pub in your neighborhood. The next time you go out with friends, you can enjoy a night away from the hustle of a bar and relax in a pub instead. If you don’t like the atmosphere of a pub, look for a Spanish tavern called a taberna or tapas bar, which can be found in many larger American cities, such as Boston and San Francisco. These establishments serve regional Spanish cuisine and have extensive cocktail and wine lists. If you can't go to one of these places, try imported alcohol instead. France and Italy are known for their wines, so try a bottle of French or Italian wine. Drink imported beer, such as Guinness from Ireland, Chimay from Belgium, Carlsberg from Denmark, Nastro Azzurro from Italy, or Heineken from the Netherlands. While many European countries broadcast American shows, they also have a lot of their own television. Whether it’s a German soap opera like "Verbotene Liebe" or a British crime drama like "Sherlock", you can try watching shows filmed in other countries. Many of them can be found online on streaming networks or services like Netflix. There are many options across Europe. England has great shows like the sci-fi megahit "Doctor Who" and the thriller "Luther", Denmark has the political drama "Borgen", and France has the horror drama "The Returned", to name just a few. If you are not a TV person, try watching some foreign films instead. There are many great international films shown in American art houses or independent theaters. You can also look for European or country-based film festivals in your area, such as the Boston French Film Festival in Massachusetts or the Nuovo Cinema Italiano Film Festival in Charleston, South Carolina. Even though Europeans and Americans dress similarly, there are some things you can do to appear more European. European style is typically more elegant than American style, but young Europeans now also wear a more casual style. Dress classically and simply. Avoid over-the-top ensembles or overly casual outfits. Check out the fashion weeks in London and Paris, on and off the runway, for tips on how fashionable men and women in Europe dress. Try stores like H&M and Urban Outfitters. H&M is a Swedish company that is popular all over Europe. Urban Outfitters has spread overseas, and many of their styles fit the European aesthetic. If you are a guy, make sure your clothes fit well. Avoid bright colors and shorts unless you are at the beach. Try wearing a well-fitted polo shirt with a good pair of jeans. For going out at night, you can try an earthy-colored button-up shirt or a sweater with a dark pair of jeans. You can even add a scarf to complete any outfit. European women are known for their style, especially the French. Whether they are going to the grocery store or taking a walk with their children, French women are always well-dressed, often in skirts, dresses, and heels. Keep your fashion simple but elegant. Wear a pair of skinny jeans in black or red, a dressier sweater, a scarf or a long necklace, and a handbag. Complete your outfit with designer heels or boots, and you will look like you just stepped out of a street in Paris. Regardless of your gender, you should avoid wearing sneakers and athletic clothing unless you are engaged in sports. Also avoid flip-flops unless you are at the beach. Europeans typically do not wear this type of clothing and shoes without a reason. However, wearing athletic clothing will make you look like an American delinquent, so try to avoid it if possible. American football is quite different from European football. European football, which is also called footie in America, is what Americans know as soccer. Find a team and follow them. Learn which teams have rivalries and which teams are likely to participate in the World Cup, which is the competition for European football. You can even involve your friends and invite them over to watch football at your home or at a local pub. If you are ever asked by an English person whether you are a fan of Manchester United or Arsenal, do not answer. The rivalry between the two football teams is legendary. England, Germany, and many other European countries are known for their football hooligans, the rowdy fans who typically cause trouble, damage property, and get arrested. Although the trend has declined in recent years, Europeans still take their football very seriously. If football is not your sport, try watching rugby, tennis, or cricket instead, as these sports are also popular throughout Europe. Europeans use a different system for measuring and for temperature. Instead of the imperial units that consist of inches, feet, and pounds, you should use the metric system, which consists of meters, kilometers, and grams. You should also start naming the temperature in Celsius instead of Fahrenheit. This will make you sound more European and allow you to do things as they do. For example, Austrians would say that the distance between Vienna in Austria and Munich in Germany is 355 kilometers rather than 220 miles. They would also say that the temperature in Vienna was 25 degrees Celsius, instead of 77 degrees Fahrenheit.

### Instruction2:
European pubs offer a different experience than American bars, serving mainly beer, wine, and cider, and creating a family-friendly atmosphere. If pubs aren’t appealing, Spanish tapas bars are an option in larger cities. For an authentic European experience, try imported wines and beers. Additionally, European television and film options abound, with many unique shows and festivals to explore. Dress in a classic, elegant style to appear more European, avoiding overly casual or loud outfits. Engage in European sports, especially football (soccer), but be mindful of local rivalries. Lastly, adopt the metric system for measurements and temperature to blend in more seamlessly.

To prepare your body and mind for bed, you should turn off all electronic devices such as your phone, computer, and television. The light emitted by the screens of these devices can stimulate your brain and reduce its ability to produce melatonin, the sleep hormone. Additionally, avoid taking electronic devices to bed, as it may be harder to turn them off when trying to sleep. Instead of being on your phone or computer in bed, opt for a relaxing activity without electronic devices, such as reading a good book, journaling, or quietly talking with your partner. Create a cozy atmosphere to promote sleep by ensuring that your bedroom is neither too warm nor too cold and away from loud noises. Use thick curtains or blinds to block out light, and cover all electronic devices with a blanket so that they do not emit light in the room. You can also use a sleep mask to keep light away from your eyes. Layer blankets and sheets on your bed so you can remove some if you get too warm at night. You should aim to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day so that your body gets used to your sleep rhythm and you do not feel overly tired during the day. If your sleep rhythm is inconsistent, you can adjust your sleep schedule by paying attention to whether you wake up too tired or oversleep and gradually making small adjustments to your schedule. You need to give your internal clock time to adapt to your new rhythm, but as long as you commit to going to bed and waking up at the same times each day, your sleep rhythm should become more regular over time. Some people prefer to sleep on their back or stomach, while others prefer to sleep on their side. If you tend to snore, you should avoid sleeping on your back or stomach as this can constrict the airways and lead to snoring. However, you should choose a sleeping position that is comfortable and natural for you to get the best sleep. If your natural sleeping position is on your back, elevate your head with pillows and ensure that you have a comfortable mattress with good support. If you are pregnant, you should sleep on your left side and use a body pillow and several other pillows to keep your sleeping position healthy for the baby and comfortable for you.

### Instruction2:
Prepare for bed by turning off electronics, creating a relaxing atmosphere, and maintaining a consistent sleep schedule. Choose a comfortable sleeping position that suits you, especially if you are pregnant or snore.

Consider individual needs when selecting walking stick height. Test various lengths at medical facilities before deciding. Choose a stick that fits your functional requirements and preferences. This will also soothe any inflammation that may have been caused by the heat. When a pimple has come to the surface, apply a spot treatment on it. Products containing salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, or sulfur are particularly effective after a compress. All of these active ingredients are very effective and available over the counter. With their help, you can control your acne, prevent future breakouts, and reduce scars and dark spots. Always discuss the risks of any prescription treatment with your doctor and let them know what other remedies you have tried. If your pimple does not go down with the compress and acne cream, you can hide it with a little makeup until it heals. In the drugstore, you will find various concealers that contain active ingredients against acne and blemishes. A mineral makeup that does not contain bismuth oxychloride or dimethicone is recommended.

Use a warm compress followed by an acne wash. Apply spot treatments with effective ingredients. Avoid squeezing pimples and consult a dermatologist if necessary. Use non-comedogenic makeup to cover blemishes.

Remember, when dating a single parent, you become part of a family unit. You need to ensure that you are comfortable with their family culture. Pay close attention to how your partner interacts with their child and make sure you feel good about how they function as a family. Feeling uncomfortable doesn’t necessarily mean you think your partner is a bad parent, but if you disagree with how they parent, that’s also a red flag. You might simply feel out of place in their family dynamic. Perhaps your partner values different things than you do. They may be raising their child with a strong religious background while you are agnostic. Your partner could place a lot of emphasis on success and focus, whereas you might be more laid-back. If you are not familiar with children, you may not know how to behave around them. The good news is that there is no need for an immediate perfect parental figure. You just need to be a strong adult role model. Show your best behavior in front of your partner's child. Use "please" and "thank you" and display good manners. Listen when the child speaks. Offer to help with small chores, like doing the dishes after meals or taking out the trash. Treat your partner with kindness and respect in front of their child. Show the child how to treat others by treating their mother or father kindly and courteously. You can show kindness in small ways. Compliment your partner. If the child shows you something they did in school, be positive and praise them. If your partner has pets, be affectionate with them, pet them, and speak to them kindly. Children can sense when you are not being yourself. Many people try to come off as overly friendly or cool when meeting their partner's child, but this can actually be off-putting. Just be yourself and give the child time to get used to you. During initial introductions, be yourself. You want the child to know you as a person, not as a persona you’ve created. While you should ensure your language and topics of conversation are appropriate for children, you don’t have to completely reshape your personality to meet your partner's child. Ask the child about school, their hobbies, and friends. Many people believe they should learn about what children like, but the simplest and most authentic way to get to know your partner's child is just to talk to them. Understand that your partner's child may be nervous about meeting you. This is completely normal. Children can initially be rude to new romantic partners, but make sure to respond to any hostility with patience and kindness. Understand that such feelings are a normal part of the getting-to-know phase and don’t take them personally. Remember, having children is unpredictable. If you are not naturally flexible, try to make room for understanding in your life. Plans may change due to sports tournaments, teacher-parent meetings, and unexpected illnesses. You need to be empathetic towards your partner in such situations and give them time to adjust plans according to the child's needs. Once it seems okay for your partner to allow you to build a relationship with their child, include the child in certain activities. Plan outings and dates around child-friendly events, so your partner doesn’t feel they have to choose between you and their child. Bowling, ice skating, or going to a sports event are great ideas since they’re easy to include a child in. If there’s a fair or carnival in town, suggest going together. If you and your partner enjoy watching movies, see if there’s a family-friendly film that would interest you both. Many movies made and marketed for children are also enjoyable for adults. Plan evenings, especially on weekends. It might be difficult for your partner to go out on a Wednesday night, so offer to come over. You can cook dinner or bring pizza and have a "family night" with board games. Many people, especially when things get serious, want to build a close bond with their partner's child. This is important, but you cannot force a relationship. You need to let it happen naturally. Allow your partner to proceed at their own pace. If they only feel comfortable interacting with you a couple of times a month with the children initially, respect that. Let your partner decide how to introduce you. You may only be introduced as a friend. Be understanding of this and don’t push for labels your partner is not yet comfortable with. Remember, you are not a parent. In this situation, you are the friend or partner. Even if you disagree with a decision, it’s not your place to criticize or inject your opinion. Let your partner handle their parenting role while you observe and support in a non-judgmental way.

### Instruction2:
Feel comfortable with your partner's parenting style. Pay attention to family dynamics. Be a positive role model and engage with the child appropriately. Be patient and allow the relationship to develop naturally without forcing interactions. Respect your partner's pace and decisions regarding introductions and involvement with their child.

Regardless of whether you place the container indoors or outdoors, you should plant the bulbs in the fall as soon as the leaves fall from the trees in your neighborhood. Planting in the fall allows the bulbs to develop roots and follow their natural growth cycle. You can place the container in a cool spot during the winter. The bulb plants thrive best when kept cool during their dormant period. You do not need to leave the container outside; you can put it in the garage, basement, root cellar, or shed. The chosen container should be about 5 to 6 times deeper than the diameter of the bulb. It should be wide enough to maintain a 15 cm distance between the bulbs on all sides of the container. The container should have at least 4 relatively large drainage holes at the bottom. Drill more holes if necessary, as bulb plants can rot in overly wet soil. Most commercial planting substrates are suitable, but you should choose one that feels relatively light and is not heavy and compact. Keep in mind that bulb plants do not have stringent soil quality requirements, but they need soil that filters water. Heavy soils retain moisture, which can cause the bulbs to rot. The bulb plants can grow in partial shade, but they thrive best in full sun. Place the container in a location where it receives at least six hours of full sunlight daily. Strong sunlight helps the bulb plants develop sturdy stems and better support the flowers. If your container is too large to move, you can position it where you want before filling it with soil and planting the bulbs. If you can move the container, shift it to different spots in the house or garden during the day to maximize sunlight exposure. The roots grow from the rounded end, and the stem grows from the tip of the bulb. Therefore, make sure the bulb is placed with the pointed end facing up when you put it in the hole. If you plant more than one bulb in each container, ensure they are spaced 15 cm apart in all directions. Dig a hole that is two or three times deeper than the diameter of the root when planting. You can fill the hole with a 5 cm layer of compost, which filters water and provides nutrients to the bulb. Press the soil down as firmly as possible with your hands to minimize air pockets. To complete the training of your Rottweiler, you should teach him simple commands using positive reinforcement. This will help ensure that you have an obedient and well-behaved Rottweiler. Use short commands consisting of one or two words along with hand gestures, so your dog learns to understand your command voice and the expected behavior. "Sit" is the first command your Rottweiler must learn, as it makes tasks like feeding and grooming much easier. Focus your dog’s attention on your hands so he is more likely to respond to the command. Say "Sit" and gently push his rear down until he sits. Hold a treat in front of your dog's nose and guide him into a sitting position. When his rear touches the ground, say "Yes" or "Good job" and give him the reward. Repeat this process until your dog follows the command. "No" is a very important command for your dog as it lets him know when he has done something wrong. Be sure to say "No" in your disciplinary tone and do not complicate the command with words your dog does not understand. Your disciplinary tone should be firm and deep. To teach him "No," place a treat on the floor and if your dog tries to eat it, make a loud noise and remove the treat. By repeating this, your dog will associate the treat with a startling sound and will not try to take it again. You can reinforce your lesson by asking him to sit and rewarding him for that. Use this command only when you catch your dog doing something wrong. Do something different if he stops the behavior or repeat it and remove him from the situation. Once you have taught your Rottweiler to sit, you can teach him the command "Stay." This is one of the harder commands to teach that requires a lot of patience. Do not be discouraged when teaching this command. Remember that Rottweilers are social and want to spend time with you, which will help you maintain patience with your dog. Call your dog to a spot where he should stay. Then walk away, say "Stay!" and toss him a treat. Repeat this for several days in a row. Make sure to reward him appropriately when he executes the command correctly. After he understands "Stay," you can teach him a command he enjoys that means he can be with you. Social and loyal breeds like Rottweilers love this. For example, you could ask your family members to call your dog from different spots in the room using his name and "Come!" Encourage your Rottweiler to come to you by clapping or making other sounds he likes. When he comes to you or someone else in your family, say "Good boy" and give him a treat. Then someone else can call him. Never forget to reward him when he executes a command correctly. Housebreaking a dog can be one of the most frustrating aspects for dog owners, but it is absolutely necessary. ### Instruction1:
The three types of speeches are: informative, persuasive, and entertaining. Although there may be overlaps between the different types, each has a specific function to fulfill. The best speeches, however, incorporate all three types. The main purpose of an informative speech is to provide facts, details, and examples. Even when trying to convince your audience, it still revolves around basic facts and information. A persuasive speech aims to convince your audience. You will apply facts, but also emotions, logic, personal experiences, etc. The purpose of an entertaining speech fulfills a social need, often utilizing some aspects of an informative speech (such as at a wedding or thank-you speech). You have definitely heard the speech that begins with "when I was asked to give this speech, I wondered what to say...." Don't do that. It's one of the most boring ways to start a speech. It often meanders through the speaker's personal life and is rarely as entertaining as the speaker thinks. Start the speech by stating your main idea and the three (or so) of your main points. Your audience will remember the opening and closing better than any other part of the speech. Aim to connect with your audience and address them right from the start. Remember, the speech is about saying something to the audience, not about you. Start in a way that directs the audience's attention straight to the point. This means offering a surprising fact or statistic, asking a question, and overcoming the audience's biases. To avoid your speech becoming too all-encompassing, you need to build a clear format. Remember not to overwhelm your audience with facts and ideas. Have an overarching idea. Ask yourself what you want to convey to the audience? What should they take away? Why should they agree with what you say? For example, if you're giving a talk about national literature trends, consider why this should interest your audience. You shouldn't just spit out facts. You need several main points that support your overarching idea or point. The best usually comprise three main points. If your overarching idea is that national children's literature is becoming increasingly diverse, then one point could be to showcase the new trends, a second point would be to demonstrate how the public has received this new diversity, and a third point might discuss why this new diverse children's literature is important. Language is incredibly important when writing and delivering a speech. You should avoid many big and cumbersome words because, no matter how smart your audience is, they will quickly lose interest if you throw around jargon. Use striking adverbs and adjectives. You should enliven your speech and your audience. Instead of saying, "children's literature offers a range of different perspectives," say, "children's literature offers a new array of exciting and diverse perspectives." However, avoid excessive use of adverbs and adjectives. It's often better to choose a concrete verb, like "dragging," rather than using an adverb and a verb together, such as "walking slowly." When you use adjectives, make sure they support the noun. It's more impactful to say that a man's skin was as worn as leather than to say he was an old man. Use vivid imagery that captures your audience's attention. Winston Churchill used the term "the Iron Curtain" to describe the secrecy of the Soviet Union. Memorable images linger in the audience's consciousness (as evidenced by the fact that "the Iron Curtain" became a term). Repetition is also a good way to remind your audience why your speech is important (think of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I have a dream..." speech). It hammers your points into their minds so that the overarching theme isn't forgotten. You want your audience to easily follow your speech and remember it when you're done. This means not only having striking images and surprising facts but also ensuring everything is simple and to the point. If you meander into tangents of related subjects, you will lose your audience. Use short sentences and brief statements. These can be used for great dramatic effect, e.g., "Never again." That is short and concise and has an impressive impact. Note that sentence lengths should vary rather than using just short sentences. Your speech will flow better with differences. Also, lighter sentences can be useful when they serve a purpose, like expressing a stressful situation you experienced. You can also use short, concise quotes. Many famous figures have made funny or powerful statements in a tight space. You can try to come up with your own or use ones that already exist. Franklin D. Roosevelt, for example, said, "Be sincere, be brief, be seated."

A tasteful compliment about a boy's appearance is one thing, but making coarse or suggestive comments about his body is quite another. Even though many boys may not show it, they can react vulnerably when objectified. No boy should feel like a piece of meat. This advice, often given to men regarding their views on women, applies the other way around as well. Someone is objectified when you reduce their appearance to represent their entire being, especially when those traits are irrelevant in the situation. You should avoid objectifying a boy not only to protect his feelings but also to prevent potential trouble for yourself. Creepy comments or compliments can be considered harassment, which can lead to serious consequences at school or work. There are many areas where compliments are appropriate, so avoid inappropriate topics. Generally, do not compliment very personal things or emotionally charged topics unless you are very close. What constitutes an inappropriate compliment can vary from place to place. For example, it might be inappropriate to compliment a man on his wife. Avoid ambiguous compliments that contain a veiled insult or are essentially compliments for yourself. They are not only mean but also obvious and can make you look foolish in social situations. An example of an ambiguous compliment is: "Hey, you got a new T-shirt? You look slimmer in it." While it seems like a compliment, it implies that he usually looks fat. Research suggests that people find such comments ambiguous if they feel the compliment-giver knows what is considered normal. Do not use canned phrases. If this person isn’t on your mind all day, using clichés will likely ruin your chances. Avoid complimenting things you are not sure about. If possible, stay away from glass, windows, outside doors, and walls, as well as anything that could fall, such as lamps or furniture. If there is no table or desk nearby, cover your face and head with your arms and crouch in a corner of the building. Here are things you should NOT do: run outside. Heading for a door frame is a myth; you are safer under a table than under a door frame, especially in modern homes. Do not run into another room to hide under a table or piece of furniture; the ground may shake, and debris could fall. Hold onto any surface or board under which you have taken cover, and wait until the shaking stops. If you can’t find a surface to hide under, continue to protect your head with your arms and crouch down as much as possible. Hold on and protect your head with a pillow, unless you are under a very heavy lamp that could fall; in that case, move to the next safest place. Make sure to eat enough so you don’t wake up hungry in the middle of the night, but don’t overeat either. Especially avoid very spicy, heavy, or creamy foods, as they will make digestion harder for your body and keep it active. While it’s important to drink enough water throughout the day, you should wind down 3-4 hours before sleeping. You won’t want to wake up at night to go to the bathroom. To make it easier for yourself to fall asleep, use your bed only for sleeping—and for sex, if that’s relevant to you. If you work, watch TV, or discuss things on the phone while in bed, you may confuse your bed with a place to be awake instead of sleeping. Make sure not to use this piece of furniture for other situations if you value a relaxed sleep. You can also read for a while before falling asleep. However, read something that relaxes you or takes you into a dream world without stressing you out. Even if you think that watching TV or surfing the internet helps you feel sleepy, it’s actually counterproductive. You want your mind to be as calm and relaxed as possible before sleeping. This could mean having a cup of chamomile tea, reading, stretching, or listening to classical music. It could also be a combination of these things or something completely different. Triggers for postpartum depression and anxiety are negative thoughts. If you think unhealthy thoughts often enough, they can become automatic and even comforting. To overcome this postpartum illness, you must first recognize these negative thoughts. There are many different types of negative thoughts. The most common negative thoughts that occur with postpartum depression include: All-or-Nothing Thinking, which means seeing everything as either black or white. If you perform poorly once, you may see yourself as a total failure. Overgeneralization means viewing a single negative event as a never-ending pattern of defeat. Mental filtering involves focusing on a negative detail and dwelling on it. Rejecting positive meanings and dismissing positive experiences means they never happened. Emotional reasoning means believing that the negative feelings you perceive reflect reality, even if that may not be the case. Should statements imply that you feel guilty for not having done something. Personalization occurs when you see yourself as the cause of an incident that was actually completely outside your control. This way, you can view your negative thoughts more objectively. Take a piece of paper with you. If you feel you are thinking negatively, write down what you thought and what led you to think negatively. For example, if you catch yourself thinking, "I can't do anything right because my baby won't stop crying," you should write that thought down. You should also note what caused you to think that way. Your baby may have been sleeping and suddenly started crying out of nowhere. Sometimes we cannot recognize what is right for us because we are too focused on a specific thought in our minds. This is the case with postpartum depression and anxiety. Try to distance yourself from your negative thoughts and think about positive things. Acknowledge the things you have achieved. For example, if your negative thought is, "I can't do anything right," think about something bigger, like the fact that this baby needs you, or something smaller, like the fact that you successfully fed your child this morning. Instead of berating yourself in anger in a hurtful and judgmental way, treat yourself the same way you would treat a friend. You wouldn’t criticize a friend and tell them they are doing everything wrong. You would highlight the positive things they have done and praise them for their kindness. You need to treat yourself the same way if you want to recover from your postpartum depression. Instead of blaming yourself for your problems, consider all the other factors that influence the situation. This way you will realize that you are not responsible for all the mishaps in your life. For example, if your baby is sleeping and wakes up in the middle of the night, you should not think, "I am a bad mother because I can't get my baby to sleep through the night." Instead, think about the causes that might have woken your baby. Is your baby hungry? Were they disturbed by a loud noise? It is not your fault if your baby wakes up, but it is your responsibility to ensure your baby can fall back asleep by figuring out what they need.

This approach can help in managing postpartum challenges.

If you suspect that your drain is clogged with hair or other solid materials, you may be able to remove them with an old bent wire hanger. Straighten the wire hanger as much as possible. Then bend one end into a small hook that fits into the sink or drain. Insert it into the drain with the hook leading. Try to slide the wire along the wall of the pipe rather than pushing it down the middle. This prevents you from pushing the clog further down the pipe. Once you feel resistance, twist and move the hanger to try to catch the clog with the hook. Pull the wire out to remove as much of the material as possible. Let hot water from the tap run for a few minutes. The water should be as hot as possible and flow with a hard stream. Stop the water if it doesn't drain properly and the sink begins to fill up. Take a regular plunger and press it down multiple times to suck out the clog. If you are working on a double sink with two drains, press a wet cloth firmly over one drain to seal it. Position the plunger over the other drain hole and keep it upright. Fill the basin with the plunger about 7-10 cm high with water. This helps seal the plunger around the drain. Press the handle of the plunger down firmly, forcing water into the drain. Pull the handle back up and repeat the process several times with strong movements. Make sure that contact between the plunger and sink is not broken. On the last upward movement, tilt the handle slightly to the side so that the plunger separates from the sink, and remove it. You may need to pump like this for several minutes to clear the clog. The U-shaped pipe is where waste can easily accumulate before entering the main drain. The trap is located directly beneath the sink and can be removed and cleaned manually. Place a large bucket under the trap to catch any water and waste that spills out when you open it. Use a pipe wrench to loosen the flanges under the sink and on the drain pipe, then remove them by hand. Carefully pull the connections apart and take out the U-shaped pipe. Use a small wire brush to remove any stuck debris from it. Dispose of this in the bucket. Rinse it carefully with hot water. It is best to do this in another sink or basin to prevent flooding. Reinstall the trap. If any existing rubber or plastic seals appear worn, replace them with new ones. This is necessary if the clog is deeper in the pipe. Remove the trap and the pipe that leads from it to the wall. Unroll about 15-25 cm of the cleaning spiral. Insert this piece of spiral into the wall opening of the pipe. Turn the handle at the other end of the spiral clockwise while also pushing the spiral deeper into the pipe. Initial resistance may come from bends in the pipe that the spiral must navigate. When you feel that you have reached the clog, continue to turn clockwise until you feel you have broken through. You will also feel a relaxation in the spiral after it has broken through. Now turn the handle counterclockwise and pull the spiral out while cleaning it. Repeat the process as necessary until you can no longer feel the clog. Then reinstall the trap.

### Instruction2:
To unclog a drain, use a bent wire hanger to pull out debris, then run hot water. If that fails, use a plunger, sealing one drain if necessary. If still clogged, remove the trap under the sink to clean it. If the clog is deeper, use a cleaning spiral. Reinstall the trap and replace any worn seals.

If you spend some time recognizing your natural strengths and talents, you can start to feel better about yourself overall and will also be able to find ways to build relationships with other people who have similar interests. For example, if you find that you are musically gifted, you can start thinking about ways to meet others in a music-oriented environment. If you are not very good at sports, it might be initially challenging to meet other people by joining a soccer club. You would have to deal not only with your fear of approaching strangers but also feel nervous or uncomfortable about performing in sports. Now that you are beginning to feel more comfortable around others and have thought about your interests and talents, it is time to intensify your approach and look for opportunities to find lasting friendships. If you enjoy reading, consider joining a local book club. You can take it easy and may not need to talk much during the first visits, but know that you will be surrounded by people who have similar interests and want to hear what you have to say. If sports are your thing, look for ads for running clubs or university sports teams or join a local gym and sign up for a group class. After a few sessions, you will notice familiar faces, and you will know that you have something in common to talk about. If your schedule does not allow for regular events, you might still be able to connect with others by attending concerts, readings, plays, or talks in your area. People often linger after these events, or you might start noticing familiar faces after attending a few concerts. In this case, you could have an opening for a conversation and perhaps a new friendship. Another great way to meet people is to recognize issues that are important to you and volunteer for them. For example, you could work to build houses for those in need, read to elderly people in nursing homes, or work for a political campaign. After attending a few club meetings, concerts, or volunteer sessions and having a few conversations under your belt, challenge yourself to take the initiative and invite someone to do something with you. For instance, if you have joined a running club and have talked to Sam a few times, you could mention that you are thinking about participating in a 5K run next week and ask him if he wants to sign up to run together. Or if you've been to a book club a few times and found out that a famous author is visiting the local college campus next week, invite the other club members to go with you to the reading and suggest that you all go to a café afterward. If you are truly a loner at heart, it can be easy to succumb to the call of your couch and Netflix and make excuses to cancel your plans. Try to find ways to make it harder for yourself to back out of plans. If others are depending on you, you are less likely to find excuses to be unsocial. For example, if you told your coworkers that you're going out for dinner on Friday, you might think about calling in "sick" at 6 PM. However, if you agreed to pick up your coworker and drive her to the restaurant, it will be much harder for you to bail and spend the evening alone. Even if you are really unhappy about being alone and start desperately trying to find friends, it is important that you choose to spend time with people who will treat you well. You do not have to maintain a relationship that is unfulfilling, makes you feel bad about yourself, or is abusive just for the sake of companionship. If you find that it is still really difficult to leave your comfort zone after some time, or if the thought of being near other people or in crowds makes you panic or disgusted, you may be suffering from some degree of social phobia. If that is the case, you would greatly benefit from seeking professional help (either from a doctor or a therapist). Together, you can work to uncover the root of your fear and develop a treatment plan that may involve therapy, medication, or a combination of both.

### Instruction 2:
Recognize your strengths to feel better about yourself and build relationships with others. Engage in activities related to your interests, such as book clubs or sports, to meet like-minded people. Volunteer for causes you care about to connect with others. Take initiative to invite people to join you in activities. If you struggle with social interactions, consider seeking professional help for social phobia.

A young puppy can learn to follow your commands, and starting training early can help prevent the development of unwanted behaviors. Say “Sit,” “Stay,” and “Come” to your dog when you want him to do these things. While you shouldn’t expect perfect behavior at such a young age, starting to use verbal commands lays the foundation for his obedience as he grows older. For a Malinois, this early training can be crucial for developing a pleasant and agreeable personality. For example, you should start house training as early as possible. Regularly take your puppy outside and always bring him to the same spot so he learns to relieve himself only outdoors. Instead of punishing your dog for mistakes, praise him and give him treats for good behaviors. When he sits, relieves himself outside, or comes to you on command, pet him, tell him how smart he is, or give him a small treat right away. By starting this positive reinforcement early, the dog will happily want to do things to please you in the future. This positive reinforcement can begin very early. Using it when the dog is young will help you with more advanced training later. Clicker training is based on rewards, using a distinctive clicking sound when the dog does what you want. This sound indicates to the dog that it has shown the desired behavior. Clicker training is a very helpful method as it avoids confusion between trainer and dog. When the clicker is pressed at the right moment, your commands are clear. This can be particularly useful when training a dog that requires intensive training, which is typical for Malinois. When your Malinois is still a puppy, training sessions should last no longer than ten minutes. As the dog gets older, you can gradually increase each session to 30 minutes to an hour. Malinois enjoy learning, being active, and spending time with their owner, so most like to be trained several times a day. If you want your puppy to sit, wait until he naturally wants to sit. Then say “Sit,” praise him, and give him a treat. By repeating this, the dog will associate the behavior with positive reinforcement. Try practicing sitting while you are out walking. When you pause at a corner, be ready to reward your dog with treats when he sits on his own. The time it takes for your dog to learn to sit can vary greatly. Your dog may need many repetitions to understand the command and the reason for the treats. Sitting is the starting point for many other commands like Stay and Lie Down. When your dog sits, you can say “Lie Down” and indicate that he should lay down. You may need to wait until the dog lays down to then reward him, just as you did for “Sit.” Remember to use positive reinforcement by saying “Good dog” when he does something right. Repeat this every day until your dog reliably follows your commands.

### Instruction2:
Start training your puppy early to prevent unwanted behaviors. Use verbal commands like “Sit,” “Stay,” and “Come.” Focus on positive reinforcement with treats and praise. Clicker training can clarify commands. Keep training sessions short at first, gradually increasing the duration. Practice commands consistently and patiently to help your puppy learn.

If someone is taking out their bad mood on you, the first step is to recognize that it has nothing to do with you. It can be very easy to be affected by someone's bad mood, leading you to feel bad about yourself. Before you react, realize that it's not your fault. Moody people experience sudden mood swings, and just about anything can set them off. Keep this in mind when you notice someone is having a mood swing. For example, if your friend was in a good mood but suddenly becomes verbally aggressive because you disagree with him, remember that he is naturally moody. Consider that he has lost his temper in the past, even if it had nothing to do with you. If you hadn’t disagreed with him, something else could have triggered his outburst. Thinking of a moody person like the weather can be helpful. Their unpredictable nature can be frustrating but is not something you can control. It may help to talk to the person who is having a mood swing; sometimes, they may just need to express what’s bothering them. If someone is directly asked what’s wrong, they might confront the fact that there is no real reason to be upset. This could relieve their bad mood. Be gentle in your inquiry. Even if the person frustrates you, responding aggressively won’t help. Instead of asking, “What’s wrong with you?” say something like, “I feel like you've been quite upset with me today. Is there something bothering you?” However, you should never tolerate someone being verbally or physically aggressive towards you. If they yell, insult, or use profanity, don’t ask what’s wrong. Instead, walk away until they calm down. You can discuss it later. Remember that you cannot control other people's moods, but to some extent, you can control your own. If someone is experiencing mood swings, it might also put you in a bad mood. Try to remain calm as much as possible. Staying calm can prevent the situation from escalating. It is normal to feel frustrated by mood swings, especially when they are directed at you; nevertheless, remind yourself: “I cannot control their mood, but I can control mine.” For instance, if your friend invites you to dinner and the waiter forgets to bring your drinks, and your friend becomes very angry, understand that the waiter’s mistake is not a reason for you to get upset. You don’t have to agree with your friend or become angry at the waiter as well. Instead, stay calm. Try to mentally distance yourself from the situation and avoid adopting your friend's anger. Remember that moods, even negative ones, are temporary. If someone tends to have mood swings, their negative reactions will not last long. They will likely calm down just as quickly as they became angry. Remember that they will calm down, even if their mood has soured. This is not a permanent solution. Mood swings are a problem, especially when they are taken out on you. Maintaining the right perspective can help you stay calm in the moment, but the underlying reasons for the mood swings should still be addressed.

### Instruction2:
Recognize that someone's bad mood is not about you. Stay calm and do not adopt their anger. Address the underlying issues of their mood swings when possible.

After the hair has been bleached, you need to choose a color. The cuticle layer of the hair has been disrupted during bleaching. Now, hydrogen peroxide (a key ingredient in bleaching) can penetrate the hair and pull out the color. Your hair might now look yellow, white, or reddish, depending on your natural hair color and how long the bleach was left on. Food colors typically come in four shades (red, yellow, green, and blue). Each color can be mixed with the others. For example, red and green make brown, yellow and red make orange, and blue and red make purple. Consider the color of the bleach as it is part of the overall color mixture. Mix drops of food coloring with shampoo in an empty shampoo bottle. Add six drops of food coloring for every 30 ml of shampoo. You need enough shampoo to apply it to all your hair. Shake the bottle until the contents are fully mixed. Add a tablespoon of water and shake the bottle for another two minutes. Now the color is mixed. Apply the color to a thin strand of hair at the nape of your neck. Let the color sit for 20 minutes and then check the result. If you find the color not vibrant enough, let it sit a little longer. Rinse the color out and check it against a white towel to see if you like the color and how long you need to leave it on. Divide your hair into four sections. Pin them back and start applying the color to the first section of hair. Apply it with your hands, starting at the roots and working your way to the tips. Once you've worked on all the sections, distribute the color throughout your hair as if you were lathering it with shampoo. Cover it with an old shower cap and let the color sit. Depending on how dark you want the color, let it sit for 30 minutes to 3 hours. Set a timer when you've finished applying the color. Rinse it gently with warm water until the water runs clear, indicating that no color is left in the hair. You can use a towel or a blow dryer, or let it air dry. Since you did not use color with chemical components, your hair won't be as dry and brittle, so it can be blow-dried. Water, soap, and heat can reduce the longevity of the color in the hair. If the hair is not disturbed for 3 days, the color can settle well into the cuticle layer. If the color gradually washes out, it can lead to an undesired color result. For example, if you bleached your hair and then dyed it red, it could turn orange.

As a general rule, after birth, you should ensure that the mother does not stop caring for her young or show signs of illness. A healthy mother is attentive and cautious about her puppies. This helpful exercise comes from the English-speaking world and is essentially a compilation of various effective approaches to help you avoid reacting with acute anxiety to certain situations. When the fear of failure rises within you again, you can apply the following methods:  
S (Stop): Pause and interrupt your current action. Step back to remove yourself from the current situation, no matter what you are doing. Give yourself some time to think before you react.  
T (Take a deep breath): Take a deep breath. Consciously take a moment to cleanse yourself with deep breaths. This will supply oxygen to your brain, making you better able to make clear decisions.  
O (Observe): Observe what is happening. Ask yourself a few questions. What is going on in your mind? What are you feeling? What “script” are your thoughts following? Have you considered all the facts, or are subjective opinions currently more significant for you? What are you focusing on?  
P (Pull back for perspective): Step back from the situation to gain an objective perspective. Try to view the situation from the perspective of an impartial observer. What would you see in this situation? Is there another way you could approach this situation? How relevant is this situation when you look at the big picture – will it even matter in six days or six months?  
P (Proceed): Proceed based on your principles. Continue your action, taking into account the knowledge you have gained during your thinking process. Choose the approach that aligns most closely with your values and goals. Often, we are our own worst critics. You may find that your inner critic is always dissatisfied with you, whispering things like, “I’m not good enough,” or “I’ll never get this right,” or “It doesn’t make sense to even try.” When you notice these kinds of thoughts, you should immediately question and counter them. They are not helpful and, most importantly, not even true.  
Think about how you would advise a friend. Imagine that a friend or loved one is in your situation. Perhaps your best friend is afraid to leave her secure job to pursue her dream of becoming a musician. What would you advise her? Would you immediately envision her possible failure, or would you try to find ways to support her? Treat yourself with the same compassion you would offer a loved one.  
Consider whether you are generalizing. Are you fixating on one thing and applying that generalized conclusion to your entire experience? For example, if your science project hasn’t gone well, do you then transfer that failure to every other aspect of your life and think something like, “I’m a complete failure”? When you engage in catastrophizing, you make the mistake of assuming that the absolute worst outcome will indeed happen. You allow your fears to cause your thoughts to spiral out of control and draw illogical conclusions. You can challenge this process by calming yourself and asking what evidence there is for this negative assumption.  
For example, you may want to change your major in college to study something that fascinates you but that you also find very demanding. Because of this, you fear failing. From this starting point, your thoughts might quickly turn to catastrophizing: “If I can’t handle the new study, I might have to drop out. I will never find a job. I will have to live in my parents’ basement for the rest of my life and survive on noodles and ketchup. I will never find a partner, get married, or have kids.” Of course, this is an extreme case, but it is a good example of how your anxiety can cause your thoughts to spiral out of control and move into unrealistic realms.  
Try to put your thoughts in perspective. For example, if you are afraid to change your major in college because you fear you will fail, consider this: What is the worst possible outcome that could occur, and how likely is it? The worst-case scenario might be that you are not particularly good at organic chemistry (or whatever your new major may be) and might fail a few exams. That is not a catastrophe. There are many measures you could take in such a case to overcome these hurdles, such as getting tutoring, studying more, and talking to your professors. However, the more likely scenario is that you will find your new major challenging at first but will learn, grow, and master all hurdles throughout your studies. You will graduate and be happy that you followed your passion.  
Your fears of failure may stem from the belief that other people are scrutinizing every step you take. You may feel that every little mishap in your life is meticulously noted and spread by others. However, it is a fact that most people are so preoccupied with their own problems and worries that they do not have the time or leisure to closely monitor the actions of others.  
Look for facts that contradict your assumptions. For example, you may fear going to parties because you are afraid you might say something silly or make a bad joke. This type of fear of failure could prevent you from truly enjoying social interactions with others. However, you could recall past experiences or those of other people to overcome this fear. For example, you might think of a friend or someone you know who has already put their foot in their mouth socially. It is almost guaranteed you can think of someone who has embarrassed themselves in public. Did that mistake result in that person being avoided or labeled a failure? Probably not. The next time you notice that you fear failing and being judged, remind yourself of something important: “Everyone makes mistakes. I give myself permission to embarrass myself or put my foot in my mouth. That does not make me a failure.” If you do encounter unpleasant individuals who are strict judges or overly critical, recognize that the problem lies with them, not with you.

Agar-Agar usually comes in three forms: powder, flakes, or bars. All three work equally well, but the difference lies in the ease of preparation. Powdered agar-agar is generally the easiest to use as it can replace gelatin in a 1:1 ratio, meaning one teaspoon of agar-agar for one teaspoon of gelatin. Additionally, the powder dissolves more easily than flakes or bars. If unsure which form to use, opt for the powder. Agar-agar bars are white, light, and made from freeze-dried agar-agar; they can be ground in a coffee or spice grinder for easier dissolution or crumbled by hand. One bar equals two teaspoons of powdered agar-agar. Agar-agar flakes can also be ground and are less concentrated than the powder. They are white and resemble fish food, with two tablespoons of this form equating to about two teaspoons of powdered agar-agar. Look for agar-agar in health food stores, Asian markets, or online. The firmness of the gel depends on the amount of agar-agar mixed in. If no specific amounts are given in your recipe, use this rule of thumb: for thickening 250 ml of liquid, use one teaspoon of agar-agar powder, one tablespoon of agar-agar flakes, or half a bar. When replacing gelatin with agar-agar, you can use the same amount of powdered agar-agar to thicken the recipe. Otherwise, for each teaspoon of gelatin, use one tablespoon of flakes or half a bar. When trying to gel slightly acidic liquids from citrus fruits or strawberries, you may need to add more agar-agar. Some fruits contain too much acid or enzymes that prevent gelling and must be cooked first. These fruits include kiwis, pineapples, fresh figs, papayas, mangoes, and peaches. Using canned versions of such fruits eliminates the extra cooking step since they are pre-cooked. You can also add agar-agar to boiling water and then mix it into the acidic liquid. The powder should boil for about five minutes, while flakes and bars take between 10 and 15 minutes. Stir the mixture until the agar-agar is completely dissolved, which hydrates the agar-agar and allows the liquid to gel as it cools. Heat the liquid as much as possible. One advantage of agar-agar is that it sets at higher temperatures than gelatin, so it remains firm at room temperature or even when reheated. The liquid gels when it falls below 45 °C. Since adding other ingredients can lower the temperature and cause the agar-agar to set before you're done, making the liquid as hot as possible reduces the chance of it dropping below 45 °C before you remove it from the heat. When preparing an alcoholic jelly, boil the agar-agar first with the juices or mixing liquids and then stir in the alcohol at the last moment to prevent evaporation. The mixture gels when it reaches 40 to 45 °C and remains in that state as long as it stays below 80 °C. You don’t need to cool the gel unless you want to serve it chilled, so the bowl can be left at room temperature without melting or collapsing. If unsure about the right amount of agar-agar used, pour a small amount into a cold bowl to see if it sets. If it hasn't set after 30 seconds, add more agar-agar. If it's too firm for your taste, add more liquid. Do not stir or shake the agar-agar jelly until it is completely set, or it may collapse. Do not grease or line the mold before pouring in the agar-agar, as it should come out easily, and these things can actually interfere with the gelling process. Unlike gelatin, you can melt the set mixture again. For example, if you wanted to add another ingredient, pour it into a different mold, add more agar-agar to firm it up, or add more liquid to soften it, bring it back to a boil, and let it cool undisturbed to avoid affecting the gelling.
